questionText:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error:
'Neither the teacher (A) / nor the students (B) / was present in the hall (C) / No error (D)'
explanation: When two subjects are connected by 'neither... nor', the verb agrees with the subject closest to it. Since 'students' is plural, the verb should be 'were present'.

questionText:
Find the error in the sentence:
'One of my friend (A) / is an engineer (B) / in Bangalore (C) / No error (D)'
explanation: The phrase 'One of' is always followed by a plural noun. Hence, it must be 'One of my friends'.

questionText:
Spot the error:
'Scarcely had he gone (A) / than a policeman knocked (B) / at the front door (C) / No error (D)'
explanation: 'Scarcely' and 'Hardly' are always correlated with 'when' or 'before', never 'than'. 'No sooner' takes 'than'.

questionText:
Identify the erroneous segment:
'Although he worked hard, (A) / but he failed (B) / in the examination (C) / No error (D)'
explanation: 'Although / Even though' is followed by 'yet' or a simple comma, not 'but'. Using 'but' makes it redundant.

questionText:
Spot the error:
'The climate of Shimla (A) / is cooler than (B) / Delhi (C) / No error (D)'
explanation: Comparison must be between equivalent items: the climate of Shimla must be compared with the climate of Delhi ('that of Delhi'), not Delhi itself.

questionText: Spot the error in the sentence: Neither of the two candidates (A) / have submitted (B) / their application form (C) / on time. (D)
explanation: Error is in (B). 'Neither of' is followed by a plural noun but takes a singular verb. 'have submitted' should be 'has submitted'.

questionText: Spot the error in the sentence: Each of the students (A) / were given (B) / a certificate of merit (C) / by the principal. (D)
explanation: Error is in (B). 'Each of' takes a singular verb. 'were given' should be 'was given'.

questionText: Spot the error in the sentence: The scissor (A) / is lying on the table (B) / next to the notebook (C) / and pen. (D)
explanation: Error is in (A) and (B). 'Scissors' is always plural and takes a plural verb: 'The scissors are lying...'.

questionText: Spot the error in the sentence: He is senior (A) / than me (B) / by two years (C) / in this organization. (D)
explanation: Error is in (B). Adjectives ending in '-ior' (senior, junior, superior, inferior, prior) take the preposition 'to', not 'than'. Replace 'than me' with 'to me'.

questionText: Spot the error in the sentence: Scarcely had he gone out (A) / than it started (B) / raining heavily (C) / outside. (D)
explanation: Error is in (B). 'Scarcely / Hardly' is followed by 'when', not 'than'. Replace 'than' with 'when'. ('No sooner' is followed by 'than').

questionText: Spot the error in the sentence: No sooner did the bell ring (A) / when the students (B) / rushed out of (C) / their classrooms. (D)
options: No sooner did the bell ring
explanation: Error is in (B). 'No sooner' is paired with 'than', not 'when'. Replace 'when' with 'than'.

questionText: Spot the error in the sentence: Although he worked hard (A) / but he failed (B) / to secure (C) / top marks. (D)
explanation: Error is in (B). 'Although / Even though' is followed by 'yet' or a comma, never by 'but'. Remove 'but'.

questionText: Spot the error in the sentence: One of my friend (A) / is an engineer (B) / in a reputed multinational (C) / software firm. (D)
explanation: Error is in (A). 'One of' is followed by a plural noun. It should be 'One of my friends'.

questionText: Spot the error in the sentence: He told me (A) / that he will not attend (B) / the meeting (C) / tomorrow. (D)
explanation: Error is in (B). In indirect speech with a past reporting verb ('told'), 'will' changes to 'would': 'that he would not attend'.

questionText: Spot the error in the sentence: I would rather die (A) / than to beg (B) / for food (C) / from strangers. (D)
explanation: Error is in (B). 'Would rather' takes a bare infinitive. Replace 'than to beg' with 'than beg'.

questionText: Find the grammatical error: 'Between you and I, this decision is completely unfair.'
explanation: Between is a preposition and takes objective case pronouns: 'Between you and me'.

questionText: Find the grammatical error: 'The furniture in this room are very old and outdated.'
explanation: 'Furniture' is an uncountable noun and always takes a singular verb: 'is very old'.

questionText: Find the grammatical error: 'Lend me your ears, for I have many advices to give you.'
explanation: 'Advice' is an uncountable noun. Correct usage: 'much advice' or 'many pieces of advice'.

questionText: Find the grammatical error: 'He prevented me to go there at night alone.'
explanation: 'Prevent' takes the preposition 'from' + gerund: 'prevented me from going there'.

questionText: Find the grammatical error: 'She insisted to pay for the dinner at the restaurant.'
explanation: 'Insist' takes 'on' + gerund: 'insisted on paying'.

questionText: Find the grammatical error: 'He is good in Mathematics and English.'
explanation: The correct idiom is 'good at' a subject/skill: 'good at Mathematics'.

questionText: Find the grammatical error: 'Unless you do not work hard, you will not succeed in the exam.'
explanation: 'Unless' itself expresses a negative condition; using 'do not' creates a double negative. Say: 'Unless you work hard'.

questionText: Find the grammatical error: 'Supposing if it rains, what will we do?'
explanation: 'Supposing' and 'if' mean the same thing; using both together is redundant (superfluous). Use either 'Supposing' or 'If'.

questionText: Find the grammatical error: 'Ten miles are a long distance to cover on foot.'
explanation: When a plural noun denotes a specific quantity/distance considered as a single unit, it takes a singular verb: 'is a long distance'.

questionText: Find the grammatical error: 'Bread and butter are his favorite breakfast item.'
explanation: 'Bread and butter' refers to a single composite dish/idea, so it takes a singular verb: 'is his favorite'.
